clue.text: They're usually classified as pale little things

definitions.note: plural definition matching the plural answer

parts.note: pale means wan
tads are small amounts or little things

explanation.surface: A coy remark about pale little creatures being sorted into classes.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Classified' is not about taxonomy: these are small advertisements printed in a newspaper's classified section.
explanation.definitionFit: Small advertisements are grouped in newspaper columns known as the classifieds.

clue.text: Land that's tiny and unmatched in Scotland

parts.note: orra is a Scots word for odd, not one of a pair

explanation.surface: A tiny country described as unmatched in Scotland.
explanation.walkthrough: ORRA is a Scottish dialect word meaning odd or unpaired.
explanation.definitionFit: The Pyrenean principality is one of Europe's smallest states.

clue.text: Drat! Shine's gone off-again!

indicators.note: taken as a call to do the letters over once more, so the words are rearranged

parts.note: the possessive adds no letter

explanation.surface: Someone cursing because a polish has dulled once more.
explanation.walkthrough: 'again' signals the letters of DRAT and SHINE being rearranged; the dash makes 'gone off' look like part of the exclamation.
explanation.definitionFit: Metal that has dulled or discoloured with exposure is said to have deteriorated this way.

clue.text: Verdi lady joins e-mobile

parts.note: the famous aria from Rigoletto completes as 'La ... e mobile', so the Italian word for a woman joins those words

explanation.surface: An opera heroine apparently signing up for an electric phone.
explanation.walkthrough: Verdi's aria 'La donna e mobile' (woman is fickle) is the key; 'e-mobile' looks like modern tech jargon.
explanation.definitionFit: This is the Italian word for a lady, as sung in Verdi's aria.

clue.text: Despot holds degree in management

indicators.note: one word grips another, so the short abbreviation sits inside

parts.note: Idi Amin, the Ugandan dictator

explanation.surface: A tyrant earning a business qualification.
explanation.definitionFit: This is informal shorthand for administration, the running of an organisation's affairs.

clue.text: Actor who made a name for himself

indicators.note: the letters keep the answer to themselves, tucked inside the phrase before

explanation.surface: Praise for a self-made film star.
explanation.walkthrough: The surface reads as praise for a self-made star, but the actor's name sits inside 'made a name'. James Dean starred in Rebel Without a Cause.
explanation.definitionFit: James Dean is the actor, an icon of 1950s Hollywood.

clue.text: Introspective minor brought up in hotel

indicators.note: one piece is placed within the other

parts.note: an inn is a small hotel

indicators.note: in a down clue the word is read upwards, from bottom to top

parts.note: a ward is a minor under a guardian's care

explanation.surface: A child raised in a hotel turned out introspective.
explanation.walkthrough: 'brought up' reads the word for a minor upwards, as befits a down clue; 'Introspective' is the definition, not a description of the child.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone withdrawn into their own thoughts is described this way.

clue.text: Stevedore in old ship recruited by one of its suppliers?

indicators.note: taken on by, so one piece goes inside the other

parts.note: a ship's chandler sells provisions to vessels
the Argo carried Jason and the Argonauts

explanation.surface: A dock worker on an ancient vessel hired by a ship's supplier.
explanation.walkthrough: A chandler is a dealer in ships' supplies, and 'recruited by' puts the old ship inside him; the question mark flags the playful 'its'.
explanation.definitionFit: A docker who loads and unloads freight is a stevedore.

clue.text: Rose in Alsace regularly died

indicators.note: taking every other letter at even intervals

parts.note: ended means came to a close, died away

explanation.surface: A flower in the Alsace region withered.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Rose' looks like a flower but is the past tense of rise.
explanation.definitionFit: Went up, as a verb in the past tense, is the same as climbed.

clue.text: Supporter in fire soon accepts doctor carrying iodine

indicators.note: takes inside, so the next piece goes within the first

parts.note: anon is an old word for soon

indicators.note: holding something within, so one letter sits inside

parts.note: I is the chemical symbol for iodine

explanation.surface: A medic with iodine at a fireside, keeping something burning.
explanation.walkthrough: D(I)R goes inside ANON.
explanation.definitionFit: A metal stand holding logs in a hearth supports the burning wood.

clue.text: Outrage in chain store in centre of Oslo

indicators.note: one piece is placed within the other
the inner letters of the word, without its ends

parts.note: C&A, a high-street clothing chain, written out as C and A

explanation.surface: Fury over a chain store opening in central Oslo.
explanation.walkthrough: C&A was a well-known European clothing chain; read the ampersand as AND.
explanation.definitionFit: A public furore over shocking conduct is synonymous with outrage.

clue.text: Yearning to include partnership that's established

indicators.note: to take in, so one piece goes inside the other

parts.note: longing means yearning
in cricket, a stand is a batting partnership

explanation.surface: Wishing to be part of a settled relationship.
explanation.walkthrough: In cricket a stand is a partnership between two batsmen.
explanation.definitionFit: Something long settled has existed for a long time, and is established.

clue.text: Developed German diet somehow

indicators.note: in some way or other, so the letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: Someone evolving a German diet.
explanation.definitionFit: A seed that has sprouted has begun to grow, so it developed.

clue.text: Darwin abandons ladies group in fix

indicators.note: leaves behind, so these letters are dropped

parts.note: the WI, the Women's Institute, a British women's organisation

explanation.surface: A naturalist quitting a women's club when in trouble.
explanation.walkthrough: The WI (Women's Institute) is a British community organisation for women.
explanation.definitionFit: To mend a hole in fabric with stitching is to fix it.

clue.text: Scrub area for Ted to touch down

parts.note: Ted Heath, British Prime Minister in the 1970s
to land, as an aircraft does

explanation.surface: Somewhere rough for Ted to bring a plane down.
explanation.walkthrough: Edward 'Ted' Heath was a Conservative Prime Minister.
explanation.definitionFit: Open uncultivated land covered with low shrubs is scrubland.

clue.text: A group's admitted working in deserts

indicators.note: let in, so one piece goes inside another

parts.note: bands are musical groups; read as plural
on means operating or working

explanation.surface: A band's admission of playing in the desert.
explanation.walkthrough: 'deserts' is a verb, not dry places.
explanation.definitionFit: To leave someone in the lurch, walk out on them, is to desert.

clue.text: Health and Safety for crew

parts.note: H is the usual short form for health, as in the H and S abbreviation; the run of letters across these words also spells the answer, a coincidence
S as in H&S

explanation.surface: Workplace safety rules for a team.
explanation.walkthrough: Health and Safety is often written H&S.
explanation.definitionFit: Workers on a ship are deckhands, so the crew.

clue.text: Possibly Hague man's short break on spacecraft

indicators.note: in a down clue, one piece sits above the other

parts.note: hol is a shortened holiday
a lander is a craft that touches down on a planet

explanation.surface: A Dutchman's brief holiday aboard a spacecraft.
explanation.walkthrough: The Hague is in the Netherlands, so a native of Holland would be from there, hence 'Possibly'.
explanation.definitionFit: A resident of The Hague would be a Dutchman, hailing from the Netherlands.

clue.text: Immature flier beginning to need help welcomes ace

indicators.note: the first letter of the following word
takes in, so one letter goes inside

parts.note: aid means help
A is the abbreviation for ace in cards

explanation.surface: A young insect needing help takes in a top card.
explanation.walkthrough: The water nymph of mythology is also the aquatic larva of a dragonfly or mayfly.
explanation.definitionFit: The aquatic larva of a dragonfly will later fly, so it is an immature flier.

clue.text: I'd ranch rebuilt in Highland loch

indicators.note: made again in a new form, so the letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: A farm rebuilt beside a Scottish lake.
explanation.walkthrough: Loch Inchard is a sea loch in Sutherland in the Scottish Highlands.
explanation.definitionFit: Loch Inchard is a Scottish sea inlet in the far north-west.

clue.text: Where a salmagundi stew's GM-free?

indicators.note: a stew mixes its ingredients, so the letters are rearranged

parts.note: GM, genetically modified, is removed

explanation.surface: A question about where a salad of mixed ingredients is free of genetic modification.
explanation.walkthrough: A salmagundi is a mixed salad dish. Remove GM and rearrange the rest.
explanation.definitionFit: The Spanish region is a place, so it answers the question where.

clue.text: Jazz accompanist is called over separately

indicators.note: each word is turned round on its own

parts.note: named means called

explanation.surface: A jazz backing player is summoned again.
explanation.walkthrough: 'over separately' turns each of the two words round on its own rather than reversing the whole run.
explanation.definitionFit: A supporting musician in a band who is not the leader is a sideman.

clue.text: She's fortunate to have weekend off

indicators.note: taken away, so the letter is removed

parts.note: lucky means fortunate
the end of week is K

explanation.surface: A woman is lucky to get the weekend off.
explanation.walkthrough: 'weekend' is the last letter of week.
explanation.definitionFit: A woman's name stands for a female person.

clue.text: I'd passed over loose ends: now I'm out of work

indicators.note: the first and last letters of the word

parts.note: handed means passed over

explanation.surface: A worker admitting they gave up and are now unemployed.
explanation.definitionFit: Having nothing to do, without occupation, is to be idle.

clue.text: Last denizen of Matabeleland?

indicators.note: the final letters of the word provide the answer

explanation.surface: Asking about the final creature remaining in a region of Zimbabwe.
explanation.walkthrough: Matabeleland is a region of Zimbabwe, home to this large antelope.
explanation.definitionFit: A large African antelope lives in the region, so it is a denizen.

clue.text: English genes make her

parts.note: DNA carries the genes

explanation.surface: Heredity determining a woman.
explanation.definitionFit: A woman's name stands for a female person.

clue.text: African exhibits different Darwinian characters; each one's discarded

indicators.note: changed in arrangement, so the letters are rearranged
thrown away, so the letters are removed

parts.note: one is I, and each one means every I

explanation.surface: Africa revealed in a scientist's theory with characters thrown away.
explanation.walkthrough: 'one' is I; drop both I's from DARWINIAN, leaving DARWNAN, and rearrange.
explanation.definitionFit: A person from a central African country is African.

clue.text: Moaned pitifully about onset of Bombay belly

indicators.note: around, so one piece encloses another
in a sorry state, so the letters are rearranged
the first letter of the word

explanation.surface: A traveller complaining about a stomach upset in Bombay.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Bombay belly' is traveller's slang for a stomach upset; here 'belly' alone is the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: The stomach area of the body is the belly.

clue.text: He plugs non-British batsman

indicators.note: not, so the letters are removed

parts.note: Don Bradman, the great Australian batsman

explanation.surface: A promoter of a batsman from outside Britain.
explanation.walkthrough: Sir Don Bradman was the great Australian cricketer.
explanation.definitionFit: An advertising executive promotes products, so he plugs them.

clue.text: Showing love for translation of Dorian Gray originally

indicators.note: rendering in another form, so the letters are rearranged
the first letter of the word

explanation.surface: A rendering of Wilde's novel showing affection.
explanation.walkthrough: Dorian Gray is the title character of Oscar Wilde's novel.
explanation.definitionFit: Feeling deep affection for someone is adoring them.
